name: bluewater-22-five-marketing-companies
lines: Before you hire a marketing company, meet all five kinds.
Four of them will cost you a year. One of them is boring. Guess which one you want.
They're all made up. You've met them anyway.
Number one. The Guarantee.
He opens with a promise. Page one of Google in thirty days. Guaranteed.
Here's the problem. Nobody controls the top spot. Google says so itself.
So what is he guaranteeing? Read the contract. Usually, a phrase nobody searches.
You'll rank first for, best left handed tree service, Tuesdays. Congratulations.
How to spot him. Ask what happens if it doesn't work. Then watch his face.
Number two. The Dashboard.
She sends a report every month. It is beautiful. It has eleven charts.
Impressions, up. Reach, up. Engagement, up. Your phone, the same.
Every number on that page is real. None of them is a customer.
How to spot her. Ask one question. How many people called?
If the answer is another chart, you have your answer.
Number three. The Ghost.
Amazing first meeting. Great energy. Big ideas. A whiteboard.
Then you sign. And you never hear a human voice again.
Your account is now run by an inbox called, support.
How to spot him. Ask who you'll be talking to in month three. Get a name.
Number four. The Lock.
Twelve month contract. Auto renews. To cancel, write a letter, ninety days ahead, during a full moon.
The work isn't what keeps you there. The paperwork is.
How to spot it. Ask how you leave, before you ask how you start.
Number five. The boring one.
No guarantee. That's the first thing they tell you. It's almost rude.
They ask about your business for an hour before they pitch anything.
They tell you month one will be quiet. And why.
Their report is one page. What we did. What it cost. What came in.
And when something flops, you hear it from them first.
Nobody posts about the boring one. There's nothing to screenshot.
Here's the uncomfortable truth. The first four are easier to buy from.
A guarantee feels safe. A big chart feels like progress. A great pitch feels like momentum.
The boring one just feels, slow.
The honest part. Boring doesn't guarantee anything either. Good marketing can still have a bad month.
But you'll know it was a bad month. And you'll know why.
Three questions. Take them to anyone. Including us.
What do you promise? How many people called? And how do I leave?
We're trying very hard to be number five.
If that's your kind of boring, we should talk. Bluewater Co dot C A.
